TXT_KEY_STRATEGY_RESEARCH_MECHS_PEDIA.characteristic_corrected_fragment: . Version note: this historical article describes the author's model of early vanilla Civilization IV. It is not a verified description of later versions. Vanilla 1.61 already adds the known-team and prerequisite bonuses to a common base, counts living teams, awards prerequisite bonuses for known OR prerequisites, calculates team research costs differently, and normalizes overflow. Keep the formulas and overflow advice below in their historical context; do not apply them directly to Warlords, Beyond the Sword or mods.

TXT_KEY_STRATEGY_SE_PEDIA.characteristic_corrected_fragment: Non-Citizen specialists normally require available slots, usually supplied by buildings (e.g. a Library enables two Scientists); ordinary Citizens do not require a building.

TXT_KEY_STRATEGY_UB_PEDIA.characteristic_corrected_fragment: To a total of 50% hammer increase from buildings (forge and factory), you can add +50% from power (supplied by the either hydro, coal or nuclear plants, but the Three Gorges Dam can be more economical), +100% from the Ironworks (+50% each for iron and coal), +50% from Bureaucracy. With some good food sources you will max out your eight engineers

TXT_KEY_STRATEGY_UU_PEDIA.characteristic_corrected_fragment: On this note, there's another interesting use for Musketeers in vanilla/Warlords. Try postponing Chemistry and beelining to Military Tradition for early cavalry; in BtS, cavalry also require Rifling, so this early timing no longer applies.
